spec.full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
spec.conclusion: V(K) is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W of V(K), if W is invariant under red(x), red(y), and red(h), then W={0} or W=V(K). Thus V(K) is an irreducible L(K)-module, with the induced Chevalley action, including lambda=0 and p=2 and without an algebraic-closure assumption on K.

M_R is the R-span of M inside V: its elements are finite sums of r m with r in R and m in M. The natural multiplication map R tensor_Z M -> V sends r tensor m to r m. The definition by the image does not assume injectivity of this map.

propositions.statement: Let A be a commutative semiring, S a multiplicative submonoid of A, B a commutative semiring and A-algebra which is a localization of A at S, and T an additive commutative monoid with A-module structure. Then f:T -> B tensor_A T, f(t)=1 tensor t, is a localization map of modules at S. Explicitly: multiplication by each s in S on B tensor_A T is an invertible A-linear endomorphism; for every z in B tensor_A T there are t in T and s in S with s z=1 tensor t; and if 1 tensor t_1=1 tensor t_2 then there is s in S with s t_1=s t_2. The scalar localization premise means denominators from S become units, each element of B has a numerator from A and denominator from S, and equality of two images from A is witnessed after multiplying by an element of S.

propositions.statement: n=lambda+1>0, I has n elements, dim_C V=n, and (e_i)_{i in I} is a complex basis of V, with e_0=v. For every integer t>=0, h y^t v=(lambda-2t)y^t v; for t>=1, x y^t v=t(lambda-t+1)y^{t-1}v. All y^t v vanish for t>lambda. The matrices are xe_0=0, xe_i=(lambda-i+1)e_{i-1} for 1<=i<=lambda, ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for 0<=i<lambda, ye_lambda=0, and he_i=(lambda-2i)e_i. Multiplication R tensor_Z M -> V, r tensor m -> r m, is injective with image M_R. M_R is free over R of rank n and spans V over C. Every X_r and Y_r (r>=0) preserves M and M_R; x,y,h preserve M and M_R, so their reductions are defined. propositions.statement: There is a ring map R -> K sending a/d to (a in K)/(d in K) for integers a,d with p not dividing d. There are natural K-linear isomorphisms V(K) -> M_R tensor_R K -> (M_R/p M_R) tensor_{F_p} K, with first map m tensor c -> m tensor c and its inverse (s m) tensor c -> m tensor (bar(s)c), for s in R, and second map z tensor c -> [z] tensor c. For some nonzero b in J with J=R b and (b e_i) an R-basis of M_R the images beta_i of b e_i give a K-basis of V(K) indexed by I, so dim_K V(K)=n>0. Relative to this basis the induced generators have matrices red(x) beta_0=0, red(x) beta_i=(lambda-i+1) beta_{i-1} for i>=1, red(y) beta_i=(i+1) beta_{i+1} for i<lambda, red(y) beta_lambda=0, red(h) beta_i=(lambda-2i) beta_i, with integer coefficients interpreted in K. locals.declaration: Use t as the induction index for the two formulas about y^t v.

argument.text: From H001, n=lambda+1 is positive and the integer interval I has n members. H002 gives dim_C V=n. We prove for every t>=0 that h y^t v=(lambda-2t)y^t v and, for t>=1, x y^t v=t(lambda-t+1)y^{t-1}v. The h formula at t=0 is H003. Using hy=yh-2y from H002, the h formula at t+1 follows by applying y to its value at t and subtracting 2y^{t+1}v. For x, the first case is xyv=(yx+h)v=lambda v by H002 and H003. In the step t>=1 assume the two formulas at t (L1). The identity xy=yx+h gives x y^{t+1}v=y(xy^t v)+hy^t v=[t(lambda-t+1)+lambda-2t]y^t v=(t+1)(lambda-t)y^t v. The analogous h step has just been verified. Discharge L1 into the induction step and apply natural induction. This proves both formulas for all their stated indices.

produces.statement: n>0, card(I)=n, dim_C V=n; for all nonnegative integers t, h y^t v=(lambda-2t)y^t v, and for t>=1, x y^t v=t(lambda-t+1)y^{t-1}v.

argument.text: For every i in I, repeated application of F001 gives x^i y^i v=i! lambda(lambda-1)...(lambda-i+1)v; at i=0 the product is 1. Each factor for positive i is a positive integer, hence nonzero in C, and H003 gives v!=0. Thus e_i!=0. By F001 their h-eigenvalues lambda-2i are distinct in C. For any relation sum_{i in I} a_i e_i=0, and any j in I, apply product_{k in I,k!=j}(h-(lambda-2k)Id). The result is a_j product_{k!=j}(2k-2j)e_j=0; all factors and e_j are nonzero. Hence every a_j=0. There are n independent vectors and dim_C V=n, so they are a basis. F001 says that y^{lambda+1}v, if nonzero, would have eigenvalue -lambda-2. Expanding it in this basis and comparing coefficients in the h-eigenvector equation forces every coefficient to vanish, because -lambda-2 differs from every lambda-2i with i in I. Therefore y^{lambda+1}v=0 and all higher powers vanish. Dividing F001 by i! and using the definition of e now gives xe_0=0, xe_i=(lambda-i+1)e_{i-1}, ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} within the interval, ye_lambda=0, and he_i=(lambda-2i)e_i. Also e_0=v.

produces.statement: e is a complex basis of V, e_0=v, y^t v=0 for all t>lambda; xe_0=0, xe_i=(lambda-i+1)e_{i-1} for 1<=i<=lambda; ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for 0<=i<lambda, ye_lambda=0, and he_i=(lambda-2i)e_i for i in I.

argument.text: Iterating the matrices in F002, x^r e_i/r! has coefficient [(lambda-i+1)...(lambda-i+r)]/r! at e_{i-r} when r<=i, and y^r e_i/r! has coefficient [(i+1)...(i+r)]/r! at e_{i+r} when i+r<=lambda. Empty products are one. M006, with (a,t)=(lambda-i+r,r) and (i+r,r) respectively, identifies these coefficients with binom(lambda-i+r,r) and binom(i+r,r): cancel the nonzero factorial (a-r)! in a!=binom(a,r)r!(a-r)!. The coefficients are natural integers. If r>i, iterating x reaches xe_0=0; if i+r>lambda, iterating y reaches ye_lambda=0. This proves the full divided-power formulas, together with F001 and F002, hence N001.

argument.text: Choose m from F001. Apply M001 with A=Z, B=R, T=M and basis m. The family 1 tensor m_i is an R-basis of R tensor_Z M. Multiplication sends it to m_i in V. If an R-linear combination maps to zero, all its coefficients vanish by the complex independence of m, since R is a subring of C. Thus multiplication is injective and has precisely the R-span M_R as image. The m_i are therefore an R-basis of M_R, of rank card(I)=n, and M_R spans V over C. H001 ensures R is indeed a ring: denominators not divisible by the prime p are closed under multiplication, and sums have a product denominator of the same kind. By H004 all X_r,Y_r preserve M, and then R-linearity makes them preserve M_R. In particular x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve both. H002 gives h=xy-yx, so h does too. Hence the restrictions and tensor reductions of x,y,h and every X_r,Y_r are defined.

argument.text: Define the coordinate modules J_i as stated. N001 gives e_0=v and H001 ensures 0 is in I, so J_0=J. N002 says every E_ij preserves M_R. If c belongs to J_j, applying E_ij to c e_j gives c e_i in M_R, so J_j is contained in J_i. Reversing i,j proves equality; thus all equal J. For any z in M_R, its coordinate projection E_ii z lies in M_R, so every coordinate lies in J. Conversely a finite sum sum_i c_i e_i with all c_i in J lies in M_R. By independence in N001 the representation is unique. These are inverse R-linear coordinate and summation maps, proving M_R is the internal direct sum of J e_i.

produces.statement: Every J_i equals J, and the summation map J^I -> M_R, (c_i) -> sum_i c_i e_i, is an R-linear isomorphism with inverse the e-coordinate tuple.

argument.text: By N002, M_R has a finite R-basis. Its coordinate map at index 0 has image J by F001, so the finitely many 0-th coordinates of that basis generate J. This explicitly proves finite generation. Moreover M_R spans the nonzero space V (N001 gives positive dimension). Therefore some element of M_R has a nonzero coordinate in the basis e. argument.text: Put T=Q tensor_R J and U=Q tensor_R M_R, and let mu:T -> C be multiplication. The nonzero elements of R form a multiplicative submonoid, and Q is the scalar localization at that submonoid: R embeds in Q, every rational is an integer numerator divided by a nonzero integer denominator (both are in R), all nonzero denominators become units, and equality of two embedded elements is already equality in R. Apply M003 with A=R, B=Q, S=R minus {0}, first to J and also to M_R. In particular every element of T can be written (1/s) tensor c for c in J and nonzero s in R, by its surjectivity clause and multiplication by s^(-1). If mu of this element is zero, then c/s=0 in C and c=0, whence the tensor is zero. Thus mu is injective. The analogous multiplication U -> V is injective by exactly the same numerator argument. Since N003 says J is finitely generated, tensors of its finite generators span T over Q. Thus T is finite dimensional.

produces.statement: mu:T -> C is injective. Every element of T is a tensor (1/s) tensor c for c in J and nonzero s in R. T is finite dimensional over Q. Multiplication U -> V is also injective.

argument.text: Set r0=dim_Q T, finite by F001. Tensor the coordinate decomposition in N003: explicitly define a Q-linear map T^I -> U by sending an elementary tuple whose i-th component is q tensor c and all others zero to q tensor (c e_i). Its inverse sends q tensor z to the tuple (q tensor coord_i(z))_i, where coord_i is the R-linear inverse-coordinate map in N003. The balancing relations make both maps well-defined, and their composites are the identity on pure tensors and on elementary tuples, hence on all finite sums. Thus U is isomorphic to T^I. Apply M002 over Q, with every factor equal to T. The factors are finite dimensional by F001 and are free because they are vector spaces; hence dim_Q(T^I)=sum_{i in I} r0=n r0. Transport of a basis through the displayed isomorphism preserves its finite cardinality, so M004 and F002 give n=n r0. N001 gives n>0, so r0=1. Combining this with F001 proves the injection and rank-one assertions and says that the image of mu is a one-dimensional rational subspace of C containing J.

produces.statement: dim_Q T=1, mu is injective, and its image is the rational span of J in C. In particular, for any nonzero a in J, every c in J has the form c=q a for some q in Q, nonzero if c is nonzero.

argument.text: We record the scalar decomposition needed for finite generators. For any nonzero rational q, take its signed integer numerator and positive denominator. Their absolute numerator and denominator are nonzero natural numbers. Apply M005 to each, with its q-parameter equal to the present prime p. H001 gives p>=2, hence p!=1. We obtain numerator absolute value p^alpha A and denominator p^beta B, with A,B natural and neither divisible by p. Therefore q=p^(alpha-beta)u, where u is the signed rational A/B. Both u and u^(-1) have denominator not divisible by p, so u is a unit in R. The exponents alpha,beta may differ in either direction, which is why integer powers are used. This proves the assertion for every nonzero rational q.

produces.statement: For every nonzero q in Q there exist an integer d and a unit u of R such that q=p^d u.

argument.text: Choose nonzero a0 in J and a finite nonempty tuple g of nonzero generators of J, using N003; removing zero entries leaves a generating tuple, and emptiness would force J=0. F003 gives g_j=qg_j a0 with nonzero rationals qg_j. Use F004 to choose qg_j=p^(nu_j)ug_j with integers nu_j and units ug_j in R. The finite nonempty tuple nu has a minimum nu_min. Put b0=p^(nu_min)a0, which is nonzero. For every generator, g_j=p^(nu_j-nu_min)ug_j b0 lies in R b0, because nu_j-nu_min is nonnegative. A generator at the minimum is ug_j b0 with ug_j a unit; therefore b0 belongs to J and that generator generates R b0. It follows in both directions that J=R b0. N003 then gives spanning of M_R by b0 e_i; their independence follows from the complex independence of e in N001 and b0!=0. Thus they are an R-basis, and b=b0 witnesses N004. No claim that every submodule of C has rank one was made: the essential rank computation is S003.

argument.text: Choose b0 as in N004. For every denominator d not divisible by p, its image in K is nonzero, since H001 gives characteristic p; it is therefore invertible. Define rho(a/d)=bar(a)/bar(d). Cross multiplication in Q proves independence of the chosen fraction, since denominators remain invertible; it also proves additivity, multiplicativity and preservation of 1. This is the ring map R -> K. Define V(K) -> M_R tensor_R K by m tensor c -> m tensor c. Its inverse sends (r m) tensor c to m tensor rho(r)c and extends over finite sums; equivalently on R tensor_Z M it sends (r tensor m) tensor c to m tensor rho(r)c using N002. The Z- and R-balancing relations prove both maps well-defined, and on pure tensors their composites are identity; pure tensors span, so these are inverse K-linear maps. Since rho(p)=0, the map z tensor c -> [z] tensor c takes M_R tensor_R K to (M_R/p M_R) tensor_{F_p} K. Its inverse sends [z] tensor c to z tensor c: changing z by p z' adds z' tensor pc=0, and scalar balancing is precisely reduction of rho modulo p. Every residue class in R/pR is the residue of an integer: choose an inverse of its denominator modulo the prime p. Its kernel is pR, so R/pR=F_p canonically and the displayed F_p scalar structure is valid. These checks prove the second pair of maps well-defined and inverse.

It says 1 tensor (b0 e_i) is a K-basis of K tensor_R M_R; exchanging the tensor factors sends it to (b0 e_i) tensor 1, with inverse the same exchange. Thus beta is a K-basis of V(K). The same coordinate argument over R/pR shows the images of b0 e_i form an F_p-basis of M_R/p M_R: an R-coordinate lies in p M_R exactly when every coordinate is in pR. Apply M004 over K to beta and use N001 to obtain dim_K V(K)=card(I)=n>0. N001 gives the x,y,h matrices on e. Multiplication by the scalar b0 commutes with all these complex-linear operators; restriction to M_R and then the tensor maps in F001 therefore give on beta precisely those matrices with their integer entries mapped into K. The tensor maps intertwine the operators because this holds on m tensor c and extends linearly.

argument.text: For 0<=r<=lambda<p, every factor from 1 through r has nonzero image in K, so r! is nonzero. The operator equality r! X_r=x^r on M is an equality of integer-linear maps because X_r preserves M by N002; tensoring it gives red(X_r)=(r!)^(-1)red(x)^r, and likewise for Y. Formula N002 for E_ij is an identity of R-linear operators on M_R, not necessarily integer operators on M; tensor it on M_R and use F001 and F002. By its matrix on b0 e_k its left side becomes the K-matrix unit F_ij of beta. Its right side becomes binom(lambda,j)^(-1) red(X_{lambda-i}) red(Y_lambda) red(X_lambda) red(Y_{lambda-j}). The image of binom(lambda,j) is nonzero: it was a unit in R by N002, and a unital ring map to a field sends a unit to a unit. All divided-power indices in this expression are between 0 and lambda. Hence every K-subspace invariant under red(x),red(y) is invariant under their powers, K-scalar multiples and compositions, so is invariant under every F_ij. This proves all the assertions of N005, with b=b0.

argument.text: Choose beta and its matrix units F as in N005, and fix an arbitrary K-subspace W of V(K). Assume L1: W is invariant under red(x),red(y),red(h). N005 then gives invariance under all F_ij, using only x,y invariance. If W={0}, the desired alternative holds. In the remaining branch assume L2: W!={0}; then there exists a nonzero vector in W.

argument.text: Choose nonzero w in W using F001 and write w=sum_{i in I} c_i beta_i in its unique basis coordinates from N005. At least one c_j is nonzero, for otherwise the sum is zero; choose such j. For each i in I, the matrix-unit definition gives F_ij w=c_j beta_i. F001 puts this vector in W. Since K is a field and c_j!=0, scalar multiplication by c_j^(-1) puts beta_i in W. Thus W contains every basis vector and all their K-linear combinations; W=V(K). Discharge L2 and combine with the zero branch to obtain W={0} or W=V(K) under L1.

argument.text: F002 holds for arbitrary W, so universal introduction proves the asserted subspace statement. N005 gives dim_K V(K)=n>0, hence V(K) is nonzero. N002 proves x,y,h preserve M, and H002 gives their commutator relations; tensor extension preserves compositions and integer sums, so these operators give precisely the induced action of L(K). A K-subspace is invariant under that action if and only if it is invariant under the three generators, because their integral span extends to the K-span defining L(K). Thus the proved subspace statement is irreducibility as an L(K)-module. H001 allowed lambda=0, where all factorials and binomial coefficients used are 1 and the basis has one element. If p=2, H001 allows exactly lambda=0 or 1; no proof step required distinct h-eigenvalues in K, N001 used distinct eigenvalues only in C, whereas the present conclusion uses the matrix units in N005. No use was made of algebraic closure of K. This proves the complete P.
